<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917870_theRebbe_730" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917870_theRebbe_730__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the allegory of the beast and bird from the Gemara, relating them to the coarse and refined levels of the animal soul.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be explained according to what is stated in the Gemara:</t>
    <t s="1">A beast that was created from dry land is kosher with two signs, etc.; a bird that was created from marshland is kosher with one sign.</t>
    <t s="2">And it is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="3">that a beast created from dust</t>
    <t s="4">(dry land)</t>
    <t s="5">—therefore it has healthy and strong vitality—</t>
    <t s="6">alludes to the animal soul as it is in the strength of coarseness.</t>
    <t s="7">Therefore its kosher status requires two signs.</t>
    <t s="8">And a bird created from marshland,</t>
    <t s="9">water and dust,</t>
    <t s="10">alludes to the animal soul as it is in refinement.</t>
    <t s="11">Therefore its kosher status requires one sign.</t>
    <t s="12">And in more detail:</t>
    <t s="13">The beast is the animal soul</t>
    <t s="14">(itself),</t>
    <t s="15">which is from the lower levels of Nogah</t>
    <t s="16">(its coarseness),</t>
    <t s="17">and the bird is the intellectual soul, which is from the higher levels of Nogah</t>
    <t s="18">(its refinement),</t>
    <t s="19">therefore it is an intermediary</t>
    <t s="20">between the animal soul and the G-dly soul.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is that the bird flies in the air</t>
    <t s="22">(from time to time),</t>
    <t s="23">for this can be explained in two ways.</t>
    <t s="24">The flight in the air</t>
    <t s="25">(of the bird)</t>
    <t s="26">is from the side of the intellectual soul itself.</t>
    <t s="27">For the nature of the intellect</t>
    <t s="28">(even the intellect of the intellectual soul, although it is natural intellect,</t>
    <t s="29">intellect of Nogah,</t>
    <t s="30">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="31">since it is intellect,</t>
    <t s="32">its nature)</t>
    <t s="33">is to be drawn after that which is above it.</t>
    <t s="34">And there is another aspect in this:</t>
    <t s="35">that through the clothing of the G-dly soul in the intellectual soul,</t>
    <t s="36">it is able to apprehend matters of G-dliness that are above the world.</t>
    <t s="37">However, even then it only agrees to the apprehension of the G-dly soul, but it remains in its essence—human intellect.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains why guarding birds requires a covered courtyard, as the refined evil of Nogah is less noticeable and the intellectual soul's tendency to soar requires greater protection.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this [law]—that guarding beasts is also in an uncovered courtyard, while guarding birds is specifically in a covered courtyard</t>
    <t s="2">(even though birds are more refined)—</t>
    <t s="3">is because the refinement of Nogah is not so noticeable,</t>
    <t s="4">and therefore requires greater guarding.</t>
    <t s="5">And to add:</t>
    <t s="6">Just as in the physical,</t>
    <t s="7">the reason that birds are not guarded in an uncovered courtyard is because they can fly</t>
    <t s="8">(over the partitions),</t>
    <t s="9">so too is it in spirituality:</t>
    <t s="10">that the intellectual soul requires greater guarding because it has the characteristic of flight in the air.</t>
    <t s="11">That is,</t>
    <t s="12">since the intellect of the intellectual soul is drawn after that which is above it</t>
    <t s="13">[and moreover,</t>
    <t s="14">it apprehends</t>
    <t s="15">(through the clothing of the G-dly soul in the intellectual soul)</t>
    <t s="16">matters of G-dliness that are above the world],</t>
    <t s="17">therefore,</t>
    <t s="18">in order to find the evil in the intellect, it is specifically through contemplation that G-dliness is hidden from human intellect</t>
    <t s="19">[i.e., even the matters of G-dliness that are apprehended in human intellect,</t>
    <t s="20">the intellect does not grasp them as they are in their truth,</t>
    <t s="21">for since they are G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="22">they are without limit,</t>
    <t s="23">and as the intellect grasps them,</t>
    <t s="24">it necessarily limits them],</t>
    <t s="25">and through the intellectual soul</t>
    <t s="26">(bird)</t>
    <t s="27">feeling the hiddenness of G-dliness that is above intellect,</t>
    <t s="28">[being] covered by a roof,</t>
    <t s="29">through this the refined evil within it is clarified,</t>
    <t s="30">[and] it is guarded.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the law of an uncovered courtyard being a karmelit is rabbinic, because guarding the beast (action) is biblical, while guarding the bird (intellect) requires a roof to refine pride, a rabbinic enhancement.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, we can explain that the law that an uncovered courtyard is a karmelit is rabbinic,</t>
    <t s="2">for guarding the beast</t>
    <t s="3">(in the service of man)</t>
    <t s="4">is primarily regarding thought, speech, and action,</t>
    <t s="5">for from the desires of the animal soul one might stumble into some prohibition, G-d forbid,</t>
    <t s="6">and guarding the beast is by fencing the courtyard</t>
    <t s="7">(the place where the beast is located)</t>
    <t s="8">with partitions,</t>
    <t s="9">i.e., not doing what he wants, but only what he must do.</t>
    <t s="10">And guarding the bird</t>
    <t s="11">(in the service of man)</t>
    <t s="12">which is regarding the refinement of Nogah</t>
    <t s="13">(as above)</t>
    <t s="14">is primarily regarding the inner powers,</t>
    <t s="15">intellect and emotions.</t>
    <t s="16">For from the selfhood and pride within him</t>
    <t s="17">(from his being a man of intellect,</t>
    <t s="18">"seeing a wise man in his own eyes"),</t>
    <t s="19">it is not sufficient to fence the courtyard with partitions,</t>
    <t s="20">for even when he is bounded in his thought, speech, and action,</t>
    <t s="21">even to the level of a Beinoni who never committed a transgression in his life,</t>
    <t s="22">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="23">from the pride and coarseness within him,</t>
    <t s="24">his intellect and emotions are in coarseness,</t>
    <t s="25">and therefore his courtyard must be covered with a roof,</t>
    <t s="26">so that the hiddenness of G-dliness is felt within him, as above.</t>
    <t s="27">And since the main thing is action,</t>
    <t s="28">therefore,</t>
    <t s="29">biblically, even an uncovered courtyard is a private domain,</t>
    <t s="30">the Unique One of the world,</t>
    <t s="31">but rabbinically</t>
    <t s="32">[whose function is to elevate and raise the person,</t>
    <t s="33">so that he becomes a vessel for G-dliness also from the side of his intellect and emotions],</t>
    <t s="34">in order for a person to be a private domain for His uniqueness, it is through [the courtyard] being covered with a roof.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
